track: B (nonblocking TCP and Reactor; groups L and M)

groups.L: nonblocking TCP: kiso/net/tcp_async over the set_nonblocking and finish_connect primitives
groups.M: Reactor: kiso/reactor over the reactor_open, reactor_ctl, reactor_wait, reactor_signal and reactor_ack primitives

L.evidence: native mio test bunko/kiso/net/tcp_async (6 tests) in the Native / linux-amd64 job

M.evidence: native mio test bunko/kiso/reactor (13 tests) and tests/reactor/run.py (stress, gc-stress, 1000-connection idle load, EINTR) as the linux-reactor check

L.work: AArch64 routines for set_nonblocking (ioctl FIONBIO) and finish_connect (poll + getsockopt SO_ERROR), EINPROGRESS classified as in-progress, NativeFS handle table 32 -> 4096 slots
L.blocker: needs a green Native / darwin-arm64 run of the tcp_async package

L.work: same AArch64 routines through the Linux adapter (ioctl, getsockopt and errno-value translation added to linuxabi.mio)

M.next: epoll through the AArch64 Linux syscall numbers

L.next: Linux x86-64 routines through the darwin_syscall adapter (ioctl, getsockopt, poll)

M.next: IOCP adapter (completion based; the adapter owns OVERLAPPED and buffers until the completion packet is dequeued, including after cancellation)

L.next: AArch64 lowering with the Windows adapter

M.next: IOCP through the Windows ARM64 adapter

findings: The AArch64 NativeFS handle table (darwin-arm64, linux-arm64, windows-arm64) held only 32 entries behind an 8-bit token slot field, capping a program at 32 open sockets; it is raised to 4096 entries with a 16-bit field in this track's first PR.
linux-arm64 reuses the Darwin AArch64 lowering through the linux_syscall adapter (bunko/kiso/aot/lower/linuxabi.mio): every new Darwin-numbered syscall needs an adapter translation.
No AArch64 execution is possible on the development host (x86-64, no qemu-user): darwin-arm64 and linux-arm64 are validated only by their real CI runners.
